output.brief:
The buffering problem is almost certainly caused by the new smart-TV app version 5.2, not the CDN. In the 12–25 Oct beacon data, 5.2 on smart TVs stalls 5.9% of viewing time, while every other client on the same CDN, including web and mobile, is at 0.6–0.7%. The pattern is the same on all three ISPs, so ISP congestion is ruled out. The app went live on 9 Oct, the same day as the cutover, which is why the CDN looked guilty. The handball launch came two days later and match nights show no extra stalling. The Tessaline cache and latency differences are small and are not what explains a tenfold gap by client.

Recommendation: do not send the breach notice, withhold fees, or move traffic back to Corvane. Do not mute the alert. Instead, revert 5.2's adaptive-streaming behaviour in Kestria and pause the wider rollout. Since 5.2 is live in all markets, check whether other markets are affected. Add app version and device to the dashboard and alerts, and use an interim query until then. Hold the free-month offer. Cancellations may be driven mostly by the price rise, and the exit survey has no quality option. I'm fairly confident, though I haven't seen the app's configuration directly.
